title: Field engine refuses ordinary moves the column engine cuts: no caller segments a chord past the per-move ceiling

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
### What happened

`SdfField::subtract_batch` (`field_cut.rs`) refuses a chord whose clipped swept window adds more than `MAX_CELLS_PER_MOVE` (1 << 22) cells beyond the tool at rest, and the message asks the caller to segment the move. Since #4079 the module law says segmenting always brings such a chord under the ceiling.

No caller in the crate segments. `simulate_field_with` (`backend.rs`, the field arm of `Stock::simulate`) and `Stock::simulate_undercut` (`field_undercut.rs`) pass each move whole, in chunks of `BATCH_MOVES` moves. So through the public `Stock` API, the field engine refuses ordinary moves that the column engine cuts, and the program has no field result at all.

Measured on main dc3679fb5, synthetic blocks, cell 0.254 mm:

| Move | Column | Field |
|---|---|---|
| 12.7 mm flat endmill, straight X pass 5 mm deep in a 30 mm block, 50 / 100 / 150 / 200 mm | cuts | cuts |
| the same, 300 mm | cuts | refused (the ceiling) |
| 127 mm flat tool, plunge 2 / 4 mm into a 200 x 200 x 30 mm block | cuts | cuts |
| the same, plunge 6 / 10 / 20 mm | cuts | refused |
| undercut disc head 127 mm across (height 3, neck 12.7 mm), plunge 2 / 4 mm (`simulate_undercut`) | (cuts nothing, by law) | cuts |
| the same, plunge 6 / 10 / 20 mm | | refused |

The ceiling is reached by the tool's footprint times its travel, so a wide tool reaches it in a few millimetres and an ordinary endmill on a long pass. A caller that segments by a fixed length still hits it: a 5 mm plunge of the 127 mm disc adds about 4.96M cells.

We found it in our own lane, which segments every move into 5 mm pieces before `simulate_undercut`: three programs with a 127.4 mm slitting disc plunging 15 to 28 mm were refused.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `Stock::block(Backend::Field { band: FIELD_BAND }, 0.0, 0.0, 340.0, 100.0, 30.0, 0.254)`.
2. `simulate` one feed move from (20, 50, 25) to (320, 50, 25) with a flat tool of radius 6.35.
3. The field engine returns `Err` (the ceiling). The same steps on `Backend::Column` return `Ok`.

Expected: both cut. The ceiling's own answer (segmenting) is applied by the simulator, not left to every caller.

### Proposed fix

In the field arm's callers (`simulate_field_with`, `simulate_undercut`, and the lathe and display arms that chunk the same way), split a chord whose work passes the ceiling into the fewest equal pieces that bring each under it, before `subtract_batch`. `subtract_batch` keeps its refusal as the per-update bound. The work of a straight chord grows with its length, so halving converges, and the number of pieces is bounded by the move's length in cells.

Pins: the steps above cut on both engines; the 6 mm plunge of the 127 mm disc cuts through `simulate_undercut`. The existing pin `a_wide_tools_long_chord_still_refuses_and_its_segments_cut` (from #4079, ours) moves to `subtract_batch` directly, where the refusal stays.

### Version and OS

main dc3679fb5 (source build), Windows 11.

### Labels

We cannot set labels. Our suggestion: `bug`, `area:sim`, `P3`.
